cmnew: Somewhere right now there is someone who knows general insurance inside out, and still runs the book out of a filing cabinet.
The proposal form retyped by hand. An endorsement waiting three days in somebody's inbox. Last year's file in a drawer, and the year before it in another.
You would not be building a book. There is one: seven lines, personal and commercial, renewals in all twelve months, and every endorsement on it written to the Act.
Before you open a file, every term since the policy began is on the screen. What was covered, at what value, what was paid, and the claims.
The insurer's notice is read for you, and every figure checked against our own record. Where the two disagree, the desk says so before it reaches the client.

And the client is never left waiting on somebody's memory. They are reminded at fourteen days, then ten. If nobody has spoken to them, a call opens itself at seven. They sign in, read every year of their own cover, confirm it and sign, on their phone.

Which leaves you the part no system can do. Endorsements written properly. The renewal conversation. Telling a client plainly what the cover does and what it does not. We drive compliance here, and we do not wait to be told.
And a change you ask for is not a ticket in a queue somewhere else. It is written into the desk, and runs on every file that week.
The paperwork is finished. The advice is not. That is the job.
Client manager, general insurance. If you are good at this and you have stopped learning, come and look after the book.
